description:
Publish each per-issue lease record, the claims sequence counter, the worktree identity file and the server PID file through the storage atomic-publication function, so each has a unique stage name and full durability and the publication function is the only storage code that stages and renames a file into place.

## Background

- Leases are one file per issue, `.git/jit/leases/<issue-id>.json`, named by a `WorktreePaths` constructor, and `.git/jit/claims.seq` holds the last sequence number. The held lease lock's `apply` (`LeaseLock`, `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`) publishes a lease change by synced temp file, rename and directory sync (or unlink and directory sync), then bumps `claims.seq`, then appends the operation's history lines in one write. The rename or unlink is the commit point.
- The claims-index writer `write_index_atomic`, with its fixed `claims.index.tmp` stage name, and `jit recover`'s unlocked call to it no longer exist; recovery's lease passes run through the held lease lock.
- An interruption matrix drives `apply` through its failure points and shows an interrupted lease operation leaves the prior or the next lease; it is the owning test for lease crash behaviour.
- Two kinds of control file need the core. The lease records and `claims.seq` live under `.git/jit`, outside every repository root, which the no-follow root opener (`open_absolute_dir_nofollow`, in `storage/capability_fs.rs` after `capability-fs-module`) does not cover, so they need a path entry that opens the target's parent following symlinks. The worktree identity (`<data root>/worktree.json`, `WORKTREE_IDENTITY_FILE`) and the server PID file (`pid_file_path(data_dir)` is `data_dir.join("server.pid.json")`, `crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:105-107`, with `data_dir` the `.jit` data root, `crates/jit/src/main.rs:6576, 6634`) live directly in the data root, as the cutover scan records (`crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:660-663`); they can publish through a data-root handle opened no-follow. Repository-state publication stays with the mutation session.
- `write_identity_atomic` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_identity.rs:234-251`) creates a `tempfile::NamedTempFile` beside `worktree.json` (`:240-241`), writes it with `write_file_synced` (`:243`), persists it (`:247`) and syncs the parent through the path-based `sync_directory` (`:250`; both from `crates/jit/src/storage/atomic_write.rs:30,70`, imported at `worktree_identity.rs:7`). Callers: `:163`, `:178`, `:202` and the test at `:341`.
- `write_pid_file` (`crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:121-128`) writes `server.pid.pid.tmp`, a fixed name derived by `with_extension("pid.tmp")` (`:123`) from `pid_file_path` (`:105`), with `std::fs::write` and renames it, syncing neither the file nor the directory. Production caller: `start_server` (`:671`). Tests: `test_write_pid_file_is_atomic` (`:845-862`) checks the fixed stage name is gone; `test_start_server_kills_orphan_when_pid_write_fails` (`:1558-1617`) forces the write to fail by placing a directory at that fixed stage name (`:1580`) and checks the orphan through the shared liveness primitive (`:1614`).
- The identity writer is the last caller of `write_file_synced` and of the path-based `sync_directory`.
- The other renames in storage are no-replace publications through `rename_noreplace_cap` (`atomic_write.rs:83,101`; callers `crates/jit/src/storage/external_publish.rs:217` and `crates/jit/src/storage/init_publish.rs:105`), which refuse an occupied destination and are not stage-and-replace writes.
- The storage atomic-write primitives are visible only inside `crate::storage` (`atomic_write.rs:9-14`), so `commands/serve.rs` needs a crate-visible storage entry for its data-root file. A crate-visible entry that wrote any leaf of the data root would be a route around the redo record (`@/inv/derived-state-coherence`, `@/charter/D-17`).
- The repository-state cutover scan (`scan_filesystem_writers`, `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:819-871`) classifies each function that mutates the filesystem by the markers of `NON_REPOSITORY_WRITES` (`:608-658`: `pid_file_path(` for server process state at `:633`, `WorktreeIdentity` for the identity file at `:638`). A writer no class matches hands the question to its callers when it is not exported, and is reported unclassified when it is `pub fn` or `pub(crate)` (`:744-745`, `:860-867`); a function that calls a classified writer is not a writer itself. `assert_writers_classified` (`:913-930`) fails when a class is no longer seen writing. `OUTSIDE_ROOT_WRITES` (`:664-669`) names the classes whose targets lie outside every root, for the directory-creation scan.
- Other writers keep the two existing classes seen: the server's `remove_pid_file` (`crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:131-138`, `pid_file_path(`) and `start_server`'s log open (`:590-605`, `log_file`), and `load_or_create_worktree_identity_with_warnings`, which removes a copied `worktree.json` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_identity.rs:150`) and names `WorktreeIdentity`. Lease storage's functions name `shared_jit`, the claims control plane marker (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The core gains a storage-private (`pub(in crate::storage)`) path entry for `.git/jit` control files only, which opens the target's parent following symlinks, creates no directory, and calls the core, with `apply` as its first caller: `apply` publishes a lease record and the `claims.seq` counter through that path entry with full durability, and lease storage contains no stage-and-rename sequence of its own. The entry refuses a target outside the git common directory's `jit` directory and the checkout's own `<git dir>/jit` directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: No lease or claims file is staged under a fixed temporary name. A claim-coordinator unit test shows the wiring: a lease change applied with an injected publication failure leaves the prior lease and no stage file behind, which holds only when the write goes through the shared function (stage-name uniqueness and durability stay owned by that function's own tests). The lease interruption matrix passes unchanged: an interrupted publication leaves the prior or the next lease and a parseable sequence counter.
- [hard] REQ-03: Storage declares a closed control-file type with two values, worktree identity and server PID file. The PID file and a data-root identity publish through one crate-visible entry over a data-root handle opened no-follow; an identity that `identity_file` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_identity.rs`) resolves under `<git dir>/jit` publishes through the REQ-01 entry. Both use full durability and create no directory, and no other path can be passed to either. `write_identity_atomic` and `write_pid_file` publish through these entries; neither names a temporary file, calls `NamedTempFile`, `std::fs::write` or `std::fs::rename`, and a symlinked data root fails the publication.
- [hard] REQ-04: The PID file is synced before `write_pid_file` returns, and a regression test shows a stale `server.pid.pid.tmp` directory no longer fails `write_pid_file` (on today's code the write fails because the stage name is fixed).
- [hard] REQ-05: `test_start_server_kills_orphan_when_pid_write_fails` injects its PID-write failure without relying on a fixed stage name and still proves the orphan is killed.
- [hard] REQ-06: `write_file_synced` and the path-based `sync_directory` no longer exist, nor does any other storage atomic-write helper left without a caller; outside tests, every rename in `crates/jit/src/storage/` and `commands/serve.rs` that replaces a target with a staged file is inside the atomic-publication function, and the remaining renames are `rename_noreplace_cap` publications. `NON_REPOSITORY_WRITES` gains one class, "data-root control file", whose marker is the closed type's name and which the crate-visible entry carries; the class is not listed in `OUTSIDE_ROOT_WRITES`, because its targets sit in the data root and it creates no directory. The "server process state" and "worktree identity" classes stay and stay seen through the writers named in Background, the storage-private `.git/jit` entry carries no class and is classified through its lease callers under "claims control plane", and both cutover scans pass.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged for lease publication: the commit point, the ordering of lease publication, sequence bump and history append, and the on-disk formats stay as they are.
- Behaviour change: the server PID file is durable once `jit serve` reports the server started; a leftover `server.pid.pid.tmp` from a crashed start no longer blocks the next start.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Lease records, worktree identity and the server PID file publish through the one function
